header:
Date: 2026-09-09
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (AstraPath HoML), Renee Okafor (Infra Lead), Liam Soto (SRE), Priya Nair (Security), Samir Khan (Product)
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 3-week POC to validate latency and throughput SLOs. Main goals: agree TTFT vs TPOT measurement definitions, set p95/p99 targets for key call types, capture workload sizing and sampling plan, and outline pilot timeline and security requirements.
topics: TTFT vs TPOT definitions and tradeoffs
workload sizing and traffic profile sampling
measurement harness (Locust/Redwood bench), metrics to collect
dedicated vs hosted considerations, KV cache and batching effects
security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, VPC peering
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: ok everyone thanks for joining, we'll run 45ish minutes, agenda is to align on SLOs and the measurement plan for the POC
[00:18] Jordan Miles: yeah great, we've got about 3 weeks of runway, priority is chat assistant realtime calls for support flows, and some nightly embedding batch jobs, but main concern is latency for user-facing chat
[00:35] Maya Patel: perfect, so two buckets - interactive (low latency) and batch (throughput). we usually split metrics into TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT (time per token) for ongoing billable cost. want to confirm your success criteria, jordan?
[00:58] Jordan Miles: for interactive our product team wants p95 < 600ms and p99 < 1.2s for 95% of the normal queries, but we have heavier long-form prompts too so maybe we need a separate target, also cost per 1k tokens needs to be under our threshold
[01:20] Samir Khan: yes product asks p95 600ms sounds reasonable, but we need p99 not to spike beyond 2s for longer completions, otherwise UX complains
[01:33] Maya Patel: got it - so we'll propose a matrix: short prompt (<=128 tokens) p95 400ms p99 900ms; mid (128-512) p95 800ms p99 1.8s; long (>512) p95 2.5s p99 5s — those are for hosted baseline on n1 instance family, dedciated numbers will be tighter depending on GPU class
[01:55] Priya Nair: hold on, from security side we need measurement runs to be done in our VPC or via peered pilot in our account, can't send PHI to hosted endpoints, also audit logs required
[02:09] Alex Chen: understood - we can run Redwood Private in your VPC or bring a pilot with peered access, and we'll share SOC2 docs and audit log export. maya will follow up with checklist link 
[02:24] Liam Soto: quick infra question - how do you account for KV cache warm vs cold during measurement? our production will have warmed KV caches most of the day
[02:36] Maya Patel: good question - our measurement plan explicitly includes a warmup phase and a steady-state phase. we capture cold-starts as separate samples, and metric tagging for warm vs cold. we'll also surface batching effects: continuous batching reduces TPOT but can add micro-latency to TTFT depending on queue thresholds
[02:57] Jordan Miles: can you explain TTFT vs TPOT again - my PM keeps mixing them up
[03:04] Alex Chen: sure - TTFT is time from request to first token, captures user-perceived responsiveness; TPOT is average per-token latency across the completion and maps to cost and throughput. both matter: TTFT for UX, TPOT for scalability and cost
[03:22] Renee Okafor: for the pilot we care about p95 TTFT for our short prompt traffic since that's 70% of calls. we also want to know p99 TPOT because spikes on tails kill our peformance budgets
[03:36] Maya Patel: we'll instrument both. proposed measurement harness: use Locust to replay sampled traffic, plus Redwood bench harness for token-level telemetry. collect: TTFT, per-token latency, p50/p90/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, memory, queue lengths, batch sizes, kv cache hit rate, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:02] Samir Khan: sounds good, do you support streaming for first-token metrics? we use streaming heavily
[04:09] Maya Patel: yes - we capture first-byte/first-token over streaming. note streaming can mask some TPOT behavior because we flush tokens as they generate, but we'll record both streamed and aggregated metrics
[04:22] Jordan Miles: what about traffic shaping - we have diurnal peaks and sudden bursts during product launches
[04:29] Maya Patel: measurement plan will include three profiles: base (daily median qps), peak (99th percentile bursts), and ramp tests to find saturation. we'll run steady-state at target qps for 10-15 minutes per sample to get stable percentiles
[04:45] Alex Chen: pragmatic question - do you want hosted POC first or go straight to dedicated? hosted is fastest for onboarding but dedicated gives you reserved capacity and predictable latency
[04:56] Jordan Miles: security leans us to dedicated/private, but we could accept a hosted pilot if sandboxed and no PHI touches it. need to validate with compliance
[05:07] Priya Nair: compliance prefers private, but for the POC if we can keep data redacted and traffic synthetic, maybe hosted is ok as a first step. still need SSO and KMS integration options documented
[05:19] Maya Patel: we'll include a hosted sandbox option and a private deploy checklist. also show expected delta in latency between hosted and dedicated in the spreadsheet
[05:28] Alex Chen: about sampling — jordan you mentioned 70% short prompts, can you share histograms?
[05:34] Jordan Miles: yes we'll export histograms, we need to anonymize a few fields — we'll provide distribution of token lengths, QPS over last 7 days, and percentile completion lengths
[05:45] Maya Patel: great, we'll use that to size cluster and config (batching thresholds, kv cache sizes). for bench runs we'll define acceptance tests: e.g., run 5 five-minute steady-state for each profile and require p95 to meet target in at least 4/5 runs
[06:04] Liam Soto: what about measurement noise - network variance etc? do you recommend colocated test agents?
[06:10] Maya Patel: yes colocated agents reduce network noise; we'll run agents in your VPC when possible. otherwise mark network jitter and repeat runs. we'll also include statistical significance checks in the spreadsheet
[06:25] Jordan Miles: we also need cost modeling because finance will sign off based on cost per 1k tokens compared to MajorCloudAI baseline
[06:33] Alex Chen: we'll include estimated cost slides; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching knobs to hit cost targets. for example int8 vs fp16 delta and expected throughput improvements
[06:46] Samir Khan: how do you measure per-token cost? is it a direct mapping?
[06:50] Maya Patel: we compute cost per 1k tokens from GPU utilization and billed token counts during runs, plus overhead for infra. estimate will be in spreadsheet with assumptions documented
[07:02] Priya Nair: security again - you mentioned audit logs, do you provide tamper-evident logs and KMS-managed keys?
[07:10] Alex Chen: yes KMS integration supported, HSM is optional for private, and audit log export available. we'll email SOC2/ISO artifacts and the architecture diagram for private deployment
[07:21] Jordan Miles: ok timeline check — we want pilot run within 2 weeks, full POC three weeks total; is that feasible?
[07:28] Maya Patel: feasible if we get traffic profile and access early. timeline: week 0 (prep): agree measurement plan, access, scripts; week 1: baseline runs and config tuning; week 2: stress/peak testing and final acceptance. total ~3 weeks
[07:41] Alex Chen: we'll prepare measurement spreadsheet that includes columns: profile name, sample duration, qps, payload size distribution, expected p95/p99 goals, pass/fail criterion, notes. also include links to bench scripts in repo (we'll share git link)
[07:57] Jordan Miles: please annotate which tests exercise KV cache warm path vs cold, because our distribution is 85% warm
[08:05] Maya Patel: will do; we'll run warmup ramps and tag metrics accordingly
[08:12] Renee Okafor: onboarding - who sets up the test agents in our VPC?
[08:18] Maya Patel: Redwood SE will provide Terraform templates and agent AMIs; your infra team can spin them up or we can assist with one kickoff run
[08:29] Liam Soto: if we do private pilot, what's required network wise? peering, firewall rules?
[08:34] Alex Chen: minimal: outbound to Redwood control plane for metrics (can be optional), or full VPC peering for private. we'll send network checklist.
[08:44] Samir Khan: any blockers we should know?
[08:46] Priya Nair: compliance sign-off on hosted sandbox is blocker; need to review redaction approach.
[08:51] Jordan Miles: action items then?
[08:53] Alex Chen: recap: Alex to share spreadsheet + locust/bench examples by 9/11; Jordan to send histograms by 9/14; Renee to confirm VPC peering by 9/13; Maya to provide SOC2 link and agent infra templates by 9/12; schedule pilot kickoff 9/21.
[09:09] Jordan Miles: thanks everyone, this was useful
[09:12] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and next steps
[09:20] <meeting ends>
